Class RichTextAreaElement

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<RichTextAreaElement>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.elements.RichTextAreaElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
public final class RichTextAreaElement extends StyledElement<RichTextAreaElement>
A toolkit element for displaying styled text with scrolling support.

This element provides internal scroll state management and keyboard/mouse event handling. It accepts pre-styled Text objects, enabling syntax highlighting, markup rendering, and other rich text features.

Unlike TextElement, this element:

  • Accepts Text objects with multiple styled Spans
  • Supports vertical scrolling with automatic scroll state
  • Handles keyboard navigation (UP/DOWN/PAGE_UP/PAGE_DOWN/HOME/END)
  • Handles mouse scroll events
  • Optionally displays line numbers

Example usage: 

import static dev.tamboui.toolkit.Toolkit.*;

Text styledText = Text.from(
    Line.from(Span.styled("function", keywordStyle), Span.raw(" foo() {")),
    Line.from(Span.raw("    return "), Span.styled("42", numberStyle), Span.raw(";")),
    Line.from(Span.raw("}"))
);

richTextArea(styledText)
    .overflow(Overflow.WRAP_WORD)
    .showLineNumbers()
    .scrollbar(ScrollBarPolicy.AS_NEEDED)

CSS Child Selectors

  • RichTextAreaElement-line-number - The line number style (default: dim)
  • RichTextAreaElement-scrollbar-thumb - The scrollbar thumb style
  • RichTextAreaElement-scrollbar-track - The scrollbar track style

  • for creating styled text

    • preferredSize

      public Size preferredSize(int availableWidth, int availableHeight, RenderContext context)
      Description copied from interface: Element
      Returns the preferred size of this element.

      The availableWidth/Height parameters allow elements to adapt their dimensions based on constraints. Use -1 for unconstrained.

      Common patterns:

      • Text elements: height depends on width (text wrapping)
      • Aspect-ratio elements: both dimensions interrelated
      • Fixed elements: ignore available dimensions

      Return value semantics:

      • Positive values = known size (use as constraint)
      • Zero = explicitly zero-sized (element should collapse)
      • Negative (-1) = unknown size (element should fill available space)
      Parameters:
      availableWidth - the available width in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      availableHeight - the available height in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      context - the render context for CSS resolution, may be null
      Returns:
      the preferred size
